sources.title: The Evolution of Urban Canada
sources.citation: Alan F. J. Artibise and Paul-André Linteau, The Evolution of Urban Canada: An Analysis of Approaches and Interpretations, Institute of Urban Studies, University of Winnipeg, Report4,1984; selected printed6 and indexed14/19.

verification.note: Fresh indexed primary report text read and retained; direct CORE403/alternate fileserver404, and a guessed repository path yielded HTML rather than PDF. No PDF or full-report reading claim. Printed6 names and discusses Creighton and Careless with notes19–22; independent Davis1985 p96/n3 quotes the latter passage. Official Winnipeg archive lists1984 Report4 and both authors. Some later references date the work1983; title-page indexed witness and official archive support1984, without silently changing older sources. Selected14/19 witnesses are partial, not continuous chapters.

qcreq_linteau_1983.note: Fresh official OpenEdition HTML reprint retrieved and full28 numbered main-text paragraphs read. Original Liberté147,June1983,34–47;2006 anthology reprint is distinct. Own¶10 specifically credits Jean Blain/René Durocher/Claude Touchette while limiting Brunet/Séguin/Wallot influence on his cohort;¶11 Dechêne/Hamelin concern other students, not automatic mentors of Linteau. ¶14 Harvey links colleagues;¶19 selective Marxist challenge is not wholesale orthodoxy;¶23 Annales influence is qualified by sociologists/American historians. Existing field routes exact; no direct personal Labrousse/Mandrou debt from a school label.

qcreq_linteau_1995.note: Fresh official DOI-resolved Érudit PDF at https://www.erudit.org/fr/revues/bhp/1995-v4-n2-bhp04828/1063524ar.pdf read in full printed13–19, extending earlier metadata-only record. Own response disputes Rudin’s homogenization, distinguishes shared questions from consensus and coauthors Durocher/Robert/Ricard. Rejects attribution of William Ryan/Copp interpretations, insists on complexity and territorial/ethnic comparison distinctions. Does not directly reject every Ryan/Copp conclusion. Rudin and those collaborators have no graph person endpoints. Full syntheses discussed remain unread; historical statistics remain the authors’ claims.

qcreq_rudin_1995.note: Fresh official OpenEdition2006 reprint retrieved; selected original-1995 argument¶1–9,13,17–21,28,30–31,36–43,53,59 and relevant notes read. Full reprint retrieved but not fully read. Rudin expressly criticizes Linteau and coauthors for downplaying ethnicity, rurality, religion and cultural explanations, while accepting their correction of older distortions. Linteau’s1995 reply freshly read separately. Rudin has no current person endpoint; no synthetic person, no assumption of consensus or certification of either author’s disputed historical claims.

pe137_ouellet_modernisation_1985.note: Fresh official DOI-resolved Érudit PDF at https://www.erudit.org/fr/revues/rs/1985-v26-n1-2-rs1566/056132ar.pdf obtained. Selected printed18–20 read by local OCR with20 visually collated (PDF11; cover precedes printed11). Remainder not reread. Ouellet’s broad concern with nationally framed economic history18/n11 directly cites Durocher/Linteau’s1971 anthology;19–20 situates Robert/Linteau/Normand Séguin among revisions of Maurice Séguin’s bourgeoisie thesis and cites their exact works n19. This qualified assessment is not a claim he assigns every later Bourque/Sales criticism to Linteau. Prior broader-reading note retained.

cdng_davis_1985.note: Fresh complete official Érudit PDF obtained; selected printed96 and109/n3 plus Artibise/Linteau-specific concluding passage read, not entire article reread. Davis quotes their1984 Report4 p6 acknowledgment of Careless’s contribution, coauthorship intact. He separately endorses their complaint about missing immediate-hinterland/suburban studies. Their report’s full PDF remains inaccessible, but selected own printed6 indexed text was freshly read. Davis himself has no graph person endpoint; David Brion Davis/Natalie Zemon Davis are different people.

hc173_paul_andre_linteau_1.note: Fresh full2012 official Prix du Québec profile and attributed interview quotations reread. Cohort list and Boréal editorial dissemination credit are distinguished from his own individual methodological debts. Does not identify folk-society theorists personally; no inferred Redfield/Hughes/Guindon link or new life/career assertion. Existing1358/1359 exactly retained.
